clue.text: Swanky hospital blocked bonus

indicators.note: blocked here means stopped from getting in, so the abbreviation is kept out of the word

blocks.note: plush means luxurious, showy
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A posh private hospital has stopped paying its staff their bonus.
explanation.walkthrough: PLUSH loses its H to leave PLUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A plus is an advantage or extra benefit, the same idea as a bonus.

clue.text: Delectably absurd post-kiss frog dropping name not so frequently

indicators.note: dropping something means letting it go, so that letter falls out

blocks.note: in the fairy tale a frog turns into a prince once kissed
N is the abbreviation for name
less often

explanation.surface: A frog after a kiss becomes absurd, and drops a name less often.
explanation.walkthrough: The frog, once kissed, is the fairy-tale prince; he loses his N to become PRICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Priceless can mean hilariously funny or wonderfully ridiculous, an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Check laminates, fix one if broken

indicators.note: broken things come apart, so the letters fall into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the fifteen letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A workshop instruction: inspect the laminated panels and repair any that are damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-examination is a check, as of one's own body for lumps or one's conscience.

clue.text: St Charlie, blushing, gets common approval

blocks.note: St is the usual abbreviation for street, here expanded
Charlie is C in the NATO alphabet
someone blushing goes red

explanation.surface: A blushing saint named Charlie wins popular acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: Usually St is read as saint and shrunk to ST; here the abbreviation is unpacked into the full word it stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: Street credibility is standing among ordinary people, popular credibility of the kind common folk grant.

clue.text: Section of FBI agents in place

indicators.note: in places one group inside another word

blocks.note: to set something is to place it
G-men were FBI agents, government men

explanation.surface: Part of the FBI team is stationed at a location.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Section of' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the answer is not hidden in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is a part or section of a whole, such as an orange or a broadcast.

clue.text: You'd like to escape this career involving a trustee

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or take in, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: to career is to rush along, race
A taken as written, plus TR, a dictionary abbreviation for trustee

explanation.surface: A trustee's career sounds like one you would dearly like to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces go R + ATR + ACE. 'Career' is a verb meaning hurtle, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the competitive, wearying grind of working life many people dream of leaving.

clue.text: In an upright way, perhaps, border on discerning

blocks.note: an end is a boundary or border
wise means shrewd, discerning

explanation.surface: Someone stands upright, perhaps bordering on wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on' puts the border above the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Endwise means with the end forward or up, so something standing on its end is upright.

clue.text: Dresser, say, with care for senior member

blocks.note: a dresser is an example of a cabinet, a piece of furniture
to minister to someone is to care for them

explanation.surface: A furniture dresser paired with careful treatment for a senior relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Care for' reads as one verb phrase but splits: care gives the verb, and for links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet minister is a senior member of a government who sits in its central decision-making body.

clue.text: Daughter, outstanding around noon bop

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one letter sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
ace means excellent, outstanding
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A brilliant daughter goes to a disco at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: To bop is informally to dance to pop music, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Information, easy to digest, provided by steward?

blocks.note: INF is a standard abbreviation for information
light food is easy on the stomach

explanation.surface: A steward hands out simple, digestible information to passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: a steward serves things during the journey on a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals and entertainment served aboard an aircraft by cabin crew are described as in-flight services.

clue.text: Neighbour's grass on hedges close to Arab horse

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted
to hedge is to fence in, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: in Australian slang (the soap Neighbours is set there) to dob in is to inform on someone
the last letter of Arab

explanation.surface: A nosy neighbour reports someone sheltering near an Arab horse.
explanation.walkthrough: Neighbours is an Australian TV soap, signalling Australian slang: dob in means grass on, or betray to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Dobbin is a traditional pet name for a horse, especially a plodding farm or cart horse.

clue.text: Exhausted swinging iron? Holiday must follow

indicators.note: something swinging turns about, so the symbol is read the other way

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a fete is a festival or holiday celebration

explanation.surface: A golfer worn out by swinging an iron needs a holiday afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Must follow' places the holiday after the turned-round symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete originally meant worn out, no longer fertile or vigorous, so it fits exhausted.

clue.text: Turn away from a fib in parties regularly

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
a fib is a small lie
the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of in parties

explanation.surface: Telling a white lie at social gatherings can put people off.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to estrange them, making them turn away from you in hostility.

clue.text: Among the French you start to manage corporation

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is taken

blocks.note: tu is the familiar French for you
the first letter of manage

explanation.surface: French people are told that they must start running a company.
explanation.walkthrough: A corporation is a jocular old word for a large belly, as is tum.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is humorous slang for a paunch, and tum is a childish word for stomach.

clue.text: Fortify me in retreat before scene of Harold's downfall

indicators.note: an army in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
Battle is the East Sussex town where King Harold fell at Hastings in 1066

explanation.surface: A soldier pleads for defences while retreating ahead of the Norman victory over King Harold.
explanation.walkthrough: The Battle of Hastings was actually fought at the place now called Battle, a small town in East Sussex.
explanation.definitionFit: To embattle a building is to furnish it with battlements, strengthening it against attack.

clue.text: New note beside vacuous memsahib's plant in colloquial parlance

indicators.note: something made new is made over, so these letters take a fresh order
vacuous means empty, so the inside of the word is cleared out and only its edges stay

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
the first and last letters of memsahib

explanation.surface: A fresh message has been left next to the empty-headed colonial lady's houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: A memsahib was a European married woman in colonial India. The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially, to plant someone is to bury them, and entomb means to place in a tomb.

clue.text: After bread, gulp sauce

blocks.note: bread and brass are both slang for money
to neck a drink is to gulp it down

explanation.surface: Someone eats bread and then swallows some sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce' is the definition, meaning cheek, not a condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass neck is British slang for impudence or nerve, the same as sauce meaning cheek.

clue.text: Cut back on item of seafood – constant for husband

indicators.note: for means in place of, so one letter stands where another was

blocks.note: a shrimp is a small crustacean eaten as seafood
c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife economises by always serving her husband shrimp.
explanation.walkthrough: The H of SHRIMP is swapped for C.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise by spending as little as possible, cutting back on costs.

clue.text: Bill is unmoved and left out

indicators.note: out means gone or missing, so the letter is omitted

blocks.note: cool means calm, unmoved
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Bill is unaffected and has been omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: COOL drops its L. Bill is not a person's name but a verb: lovers bill and coo.
explanation.definitionFit: To bill and coo is to whisper sweet nothings like doves, so the two verbs share that loving sense.

clue.text: French chemist is finished driving up French road

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: past means over, finished
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A French scientist has finished his drive up a Paris street.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the nineteenth-century French scientist who devised pasteurisation and rabies vaccine.

clue.text: Is parent behind tea? It's a positive attraction

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so the words before it are sent to the back

blocks.note: char is British slang for tea
taken as written
ma is a mother

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Mum is after a cup of tea, as though that is the appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' puts IS and the parent after the tea, so the order reverses the clue's.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is a compelling personal charm that draws people towards someone, a magnetic quality.

clue.text: Rejected from clubs like Hooray Henrietta?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
as means like
a Hooray Henry is a loud upper-class young man; this is his playful female version, a toff

explanation.surface: A posh young woman is thrown out of exclusive clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooray Henry is British slang for a braying upper-class youth; Henrietta makes her female, still a toff, meaning a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-off is something discarded as no longer wanted, so rejected describes it.

clue.text: Perhaps she's cast in play without reservation in Hollywood?

definitions.text: Perhaps she's cast in play without reservation in Hollywood

indicators.note: in play means being moved about freely, so the letters shift
without here means outside, so the other piece wraps around

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged
in American usage res is short for a Native American reservation

explanation.surface: An American actress is cast in a play without any hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: an actress is exactly someone cast in a play. 'Without' means outside here, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman given a part in a play; the 'perhaps' admits Hollywood also means films.

clue.text: Little Maureen and girls getting treacle

blocks.note: Mo is a pet form of the name Maureen
lasses are girls or young women

explanation.surface: Young Maureen and her friends are handed sticky syrup.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark syrup drained from sugar, the American word for what Britons call black treacle.

clue.text: Museum hosting popular bar

indicators.note: a host holds guests within, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Mus is the abbreviation for museum
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A museum holds a fashionable bar for visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' is a preposition meaning except, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Minus can mean without or except, as in all of them minus one, matching bar as except.

clue.text: Stumble, therefore returning for exam at Cambridge

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: to trip is to stumble
so means therefore

explanation.surface: A student trips up and so heads back for an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tripos is the honours degree examination at the University of Cambridge.

clue.text: See what fake diamond is

blocks.note: a fake diamond is not the real thing
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Someone invites us to spot the giveaway sign of a counterfeit gem.
explanation.walkthrough: A fake diamond is 'not ice', using the slang word for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To notice something is to see or perceive it, a straight synonym for see as a verb.

clue.text: I am following public beginning to earn beyond what's usual

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the words before it go second
the beginning of a word is its first letter, which alone is taken

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
I'm is the contraction of I am
the first letter of earn

explanation.surface: A worker in the public eye starts to earn more than normal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts I am after the word for public.
explanation.definitionFit: Working overtime means working past the normal hours, beyond the usual limit.

clue.text: Surface repairs? Small man needs loads

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a king is a man, a piece in chess
rafts of things are large numbers of them, loads

explanation.surface: A little workman needs lots of materials to fix a road surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is a chess piece here, a common crossword device.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin grafts repair damaged skin, which is the body's outer surface, hence the playful question mark.

clue.text: Do bear losing second-class

indicators.note: losing something means it is gone, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: to brook is to tolerate or bear
B is the grade below A, second class

explanation.surface: An instruction to make a bear demote itself from first rank.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOK without B leaves ROOK. 'Do' looks like a party or a verb meaning perform; it means cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for swindling them, and to rook someone is to cheat or overcharge.
